title.narrative: Supporting life-saving emergency and specialized health services in earthquake-affected areas in northwestern Syria

description.narrative: Improving access to general, secondary and tertiary healthcare services, including the essential healthcare package, for IDPs and host communities in earthquake-affected areas, contributing to life-saving dialysis activities for the 20 centers, ensuring continuity of care through an effective referral system, maintaining the capacity and functionality of the health system to prepare for, prevent, detect and respond rapidly to public health events, including disease outbreaks and natural disasters, ensuring the quality of the medical supply chain to ensure the availability of essential medicines and supplies, aligning the health information management system through the implementation of the District Health Information Software (DHIS2) K, and addressing the weakness of effective health governance by supporting technical bodies such as field technical teams and supervisory teams. These teams play a critical role in planning, implementing, providing supportive supervision and evaluating healthcare services in northwest Syria.

Strengthening primary, secondary and tertiary specialized health services for those affected by the earthquake in northwestern Syria and covering the operational costs of project staff, conducting supervisory visits by the field supervision team to ensure the implementation of WHO standard protocols and the quality of service, securing medical supplies, medicines and blood dialysis kits for kidney dialysis patients to continue providing specialized services

The project is an urgent medical support divided into two parts: The first part: aims to support the gaps related to supporting health centers and facilities in the northern Aleppo region, by covering the salaries of cadres and supporting the purchase of operational costs to ensure the continuity of providing services in the region, which has a population of more than one million people, and includes more than 50 health facilities, some of which are closed and others operate with weak capacity due to the reduction of support for a significant percentage of health facilities as a result of the lack of funding allocated to the region. The second part: includes the purchase of medicines and medical supplies for the most important facilities in northwestern Syria to ensure the availability of basic medicines and supplies and the continuation of providing services to beneficiaries of these centers with high quality. The project also includes securing blood dialysis kits and essential medicines needed for kidney dialysis centers in northwestern Syria to continue providing kidney dialysis sessions to beneficiaries of the services of these centers.
